s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring
50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD
Minimum lumen area of 5.92 mm2 in proximal LAD, with plaque burden of 74%

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Previous episodes of syncope and palpitations, possible obstructive component

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent syncope and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, possible right ventricular involvement

raw.rationale: The patient experienced syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis, and 24-hour Holter monitoring recorded polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode, indicating a cardiac arrhythmia as the likely cause of symptoms.

rejected.label: Coronary Artery Disease
rejected.why: Although the patient has significant coronary artery stenosis, the normal troponin levels and lack of chest pain or shortness of breath suggest that coronary artery disease is not the primary cause of the patient's syncope.
